intro: Same sky, different lens. This is the part of the universe where I stop talking about pipelines and start talking about the things that keep me curious: the night sky, loud music, competitive games, a piano and a swimming pool.

clusters.title: Astronomy
clusters.blurb: The reason this whole site looks the way it does. I just bought my first telescope and I am still learning what it can do. Favourite things out there: black holes, pulsars and nebulae — anything that makes the universe feel enormous.
items: Favourite nebula: Carina, a whole nursery of stars in one field
Black holes and pulsars: the most extreme physics you can point at
Following every JWST release as it drops
First telescope, freshly unboxed; observing from Mexico City
Reads: Aristotle’s Metaphysics, Spinoza’s Ethics and astronomy popular science

clusters.title: Music
clusters.blurb: Music runs in the background of everything I do; it is closer to a habit than a hobby. I have played piano since I was ten.
items: Michael Jackson is my main artist — Dangerous (1991), and Remember the Time on repeat
Led Zeppelin — The Song Remains the Same (1976)
Piano since age 10, intermediate level; played once at ITAM’s Raúl Baillères auditorium

clusters.title: Gaming
clusters.blurb: Games taught me systems thinking before any class did. Competitive when it counts, completionist the rest of the time.
items: Rainbow Six Siege on PC: reached Champion two seasons ago, and Diamond back when it was the top tier; still my most-played game
Halo is my favourite saga — every game finished, every achievement unlocked on console
Minecraft, Call of Duty Black Ops I and II

clusters.title: Swimming
clusters.blurb: Swimming since I was eight. The one place where nobody can send a notification.
items: Still the best way to think about a hard problem

funFacts: The stars in the hero are real: they are computed from a bright-star catalogue for the sky above Mexico City at the moment you open the page.
Fonts, scripts and images are all self-hosted. The only outside request is an anonymous, cookieless page count.
I built my own offline voice-dictation tool (WhisperFlow) because I wanted push-to-talk that never leaves my machine. I dictated the answers that shaped this page with it.
